patient_summary: 65-year-old man seen for osteoarthritis, foul-smelling urine, no pain or difficulty with urination, urine dipstick with trace blood (asymptomatic bacteriuria per Morgan 2021 Results; Figure legend, vignette D).
pretest_source: Morgan 2021 Table 3, UTI pretest evidence range 0-1%; lower end 0 replaced by 0.1%; point = log-odds midpoint of 0.1% and 1%. The 0.1% replacement is by analogy with Morgan's 0% to 0.1% response rule (p749); Morgan applies that rule to practitioner responses, not to evidence-range endpoints. The 0.1% lower edge is a convention, independent of the analysis clipping bounds (1e-5).
conditional_independence: Each case applies a single likelihood ratio (the LR for the result shown) to a single pretest probability, so no conditional-independence assumption is needed. If findings were ever combined, the LRs would be multiplied assuming conditional independence given disease status.
notes: Zero endpoints handled. The printed bands keep their 0 lower bound. The target is 'urinary tract infection', the question Morgan's respondents answered (abstract p747, Results p750, Tables 3 and 4 p752); the vignette itself describes asymptomatic bacteriuria (Results p750). The word bacteriuria is deliberately kept out of the diagnosis string shown to models.
